title: Tenant-affinity hot-warm prefetch onboarding for embedding model variants
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Implement a controlled onboarding and versioning path for new embedding model variants that combines tenant-affinity routing with a hot-warm prefetch strategy to improve reranker quality while bounding tail latency and cost. Goals: 1) Allow per-tenant affinity to newer model variants while keeping most traffic on stable quantized warm variants; 2) Reduce first-token/stall latency for tenants moved to a new variant by proactively warming KV caches and model instances; 3) Provide predictable rollback and deprecation primitives; 4) Collect robust quality telemetry for reranking downstream to decide graduations. Success metrics: - 95th percentile endpoint latency increase <= 15% during phased rollout - Cold-start tail latency for warmed tenants reduced by >= 40% - Regression detection: mean rerank NDCG drop <= 0.5 points during canary + shadow stages - Cost delta per token within target budget (+/- 12%) Approach: - Model variants: hot (full-precision or lightly quantized, low-concurrency) and warm (highly-quantized, high-concurrency). - Routing: per-tenant affinity key stored in Catalog; new tenants opt-in; rollout controlled via percent gates and tenant cohorts. - Prefetch: when a tenant is moved to hot variant, orchestrator triggers a warm-up job that does: (a) KV cache prefill with representative prefixes from tenant activity logs; (b) spin up 1-2 hot instances in the tenant's region; (c) run smoke generations to populate JIT/code paths. - Autoscaling and cost controls: limit hot pool size per-tenant and fallback routing to warm variant on capacity pressure. - Telemetry & gating: add per-tenant rerank quality probes (NDCG/precision on stored eval sets), latency SLO alarms, and cost burn-rate alerts. Rollout Plan: 1) Internal shadow for 10 internal tenants (week 1) - collect quality and latency telemetry; 2) Canary 1: 1% tenant cohort with hot-prefetch, monitor 48h - auto-rollback if quality or latency thresholds breached; 3) Canary 2: 10% cohort with staged warm-up scripts; 4) Gradual ramp to 50% with staggered deprecation of old quantized warm variants and conversion to recommended alias strategy; 5) Full graduation and API alias update plus deprecation notice. Fallbacks & Safety: - Automatically divert to warm variant if hot pool CPU/GPU pressure or network anomalies detected - Tenant-level kill-switch in Console for immediate rollback - Soft alias that allows per-request override to warm variant for critical customers Testing & validation: - End-to-end smoke tests in staging that include KV prefill verification - Load tests to measure warm pool scaling and tail latency under synthetic rerank workloads - Shadow evaluations against production embeddings store to compute NDCG deltas - Post-deploy runbook documenting rollback, migration steps, and cost reclamation. Artifacts & Links: - Design doc: https://confluence.internal.redwood/embeddings/hot-warm-prefetch (internal) - Perf dashboard (staging): https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/embeddings-hotwarm - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4821 - Eval harness branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/compare/hot-warm-onboard Open questions / trade-offs: - How large should the representative prefix set be for KV prefill to be effective without excessive cost? (trade-off between prefill cost and cold-latency reduction) - Should we expose tenant opt-in at Console level or automatically enroll based on heuristics (usage, SLA tier)? - Quantized warm variant compatibility: need a lightweight contract test for embedding vector distribution shifts.
